arxiv-2012-13955.title: Generalized Categorisation of Digital Pathology Whole Image Slides using Unsupervised Learning
arxiv-2012-13955.creator: Mostafa Ibrahim
arxiv-2012-13955.description: Abstract This project aims to break down large pathology images into small tiles and then cluster those tiles into distinct groups without the knowledge of true labels, our analysis shows how difficult certain aspects of clustering tumorous and non-tumorous cells can be and also shows that comparing the results of different unsupervised approaches is not a trivial task.

arxiv-2103-07070.title: Incoherent control of optical signals; quantum heat engine approach
arxiv-2103-07070.creator: Md Qutubuddin and Konstantin E. Dorfman
arxiv-2103-07070.description: Abstract Optical pump-probe signals can be viewed as work done by the matter while transferring the energy between two coherent baths (from pump to probe). In thermodynamics a heat engine, such as laser, is a device which performs similar work but operating between two thermal baths.

arxiv-2202-06808.title: Suslin homology via cycles with modulus and applications
arxiv-2202-06808.creator: Federico Binda, Amalendu Krishna
arxiv-2202-06808.description: Abstract 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 14C25; Secondary 14F42, 19E15 Abstract. We show that for a smooth projective variety X over a field k and a reduced effective Cartier divisor D\subset X , the Chow group of 0-cycles with modulus {\rm CH}_{0}(X|D) coincides with the Suslin homology H^{S}_{0}(X\setminus D) under some necessary conditions on k and D .

arxiv-2207-01912.title: The Anomalous Magnetic Moment of the Muon: Beyond the Standard Model via Chiral Enhancement
arxiv-2207-01912.creator: Andreas Crivellin \from ins:x \from ins:y and Martin Hoferichter \from ins:z
arxiv-2207-01912.description: Abstract The anomalous magnetic moment of the muon displays a 4.2 ​ σ 4.2\sigma tension with the Standard-Model prediction, if e + ​ e − → hadrons e^{+}e^{-}\to\text{hadrons} data are used for hadronic vacuum polarization. In these proceedings we review possible explanations of this anomaly in terms of heavy new particles.

arxiv-2305-02921.title: On the Closed-form Weight Enumeration of Polar Codes: 1.5 d d -weight codewords ∗ These authors contributed equally (Corresponding author: Vlad-Florin Drăgoi).
arxiv-2305-02921.creator: Mohammad Rowshan ∗† , Vlad-Florin Drăgoi ∗‡ , and Jinhong Yuan † , Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2305-02921.description: Abstract The weight distribution of error correction codes is a critical determinant of their error-correcting performance, making enumeration of utmost importance. In the case of polar codes, the minimum weight w min \w_{\min} (which is equal to minimum distance d d ) is the only weight for which an explicit enumerator formula is currently available.

arxiv-2309-03759.title: M(otion)-mode Based Prediction of Ejection Fraction using Echocardiograms
arxiv-2309-03759.creator: Ece Ozkan* (✉), Thomas M. Sutter* (✉), Yurong Hu, Sebastian Balzer, Julia E. Vogt
arxiv-2309-03759.description: Abstract Early detection of cardiac dysfunction through routine screening is vital for diagnosing cardiovascular diseases. An important metric of cardiac function is the left ventricular ejection fraction (EF), where lower EF is associated with cardiomyopathy. Echocardiography is a popular diagnostic tool in cardiology, with ultrasound being a low-cost, real-time, and non-ionizing technology.

arxiv-2402-08949.title: Unraveling the emergence of quantum state designs in systems with symmetry
arxiv-2402-08949.creator: Naga Dileep Varikuti, Soumik Bandyopadhyay
arxiv-2402-08949.description: Abstract Quantum state designs, by enabling an efficient sampling of random quantum states, play a quintessential role in devising and benchmarking various quantum protocols with broad applications ranging from circuit designs to black hole physics. Symmetries, on the other hand, are expected to reduce the randomness of a state.

arxiv-2402-13170.title: Improved Space Bounds for Subset Sum
arxiv-2402-13170.creator: Tatiana Belova, Nikolai Chukhin, Alexander S. Kulikov, Ivan Mihajlin
arxiv-2402-13170.description: Abstract More than 40 years ago, Schroeppel and Shamir presented an algorithm that solves the Subset Sum problem for n n integers in time O ∗ ​ ( 2 0.5 ​ n ) O^{*}(2^{0.5n}) and space O ∗ ​ ( 2 0.25 ​ n ) O^{*}(2^{0.25n}) .

arxiv-2406-06451.title: Insights from Social Shaping Theory: The Appropriation of Large Language Models in an Undergraduate Programming Course
arxiv-2406-06451.creator: Aadarsh Padiyath, Xinying Hou, Amy Pang, Diego Viramontes Vargas, Xingjian Gu, Tamara Nelson-Fromm, Zihan Wu, Mark Guzdial, Barbara Ericson
arxiv-2406-06451.description: Abstract . The capability of large language models (LLMs) to generate, debug, and explain code has sparked the interest of researchers and educators in undergraduate programming, with many anticipating their transformative potential in programming education. However, decisions about why and how to use LLMs in programming education may involve more than just the assessment of an LLM’s technical capabilities.

arxiv-2501-05827.description: Abstract . Let Q n = { 0 , 1 } n Q_{n}=\{0,1\}^{n} be a hypercube graph. The initial segment I k ⊆ Q n I_{k}\subseteq Q_{n} is the subset consisting of the first k k vertices of Q n Q_{n} in the binary order.

arxiv-2601-14949.title: What Should I Cite? A RAG Benchmark for Academic Citation Prediction Conference: Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026; April 13–17, 2026; Dubai, United Arab Emirates Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026 (WWW ’26), April 13–17, 2026, Dubai, United Arab Emirates DOI: 10.1145/3774904.379207
arxiv-2601-14949.creator: Leqi Zheng, Jiajun Zhang, Canzhi Chen, Chaokun Wang, Hongwei Li, Yuying Li, Yaoxin Mao, Shannan Yan, Zixin Song, Zhiyuan Feng, Zhaolu Kang, Zirong Chen, Hang Zhang, Qiang Liu, Liang Wang, Ziyang Liu
arxiv-2601-14949.description: Abstract . With the rapid growth of Web-based academic publications, more and more papers are being published annually, making it increasingly difficult to find relevant prior work. Citation prediction aims to automatically suggest appropriate references, helping scholars navigate the expanding scientific literature.

europmc-pmc7906923.creator: Zafar A, Wang W, Liu G, Wang X, Xian W, McKeon F, Foster J, Zhou J, Zhang R.
europmc-pmc7906923.description: There is an urgent need to identify novel therapies for childhood cancers. Neuroblastoma is the most common pediatric solid tumor, and accounts for ~15% of childhood cancer-related mortality. Neuroblastomas exhibit genetic, morphological and clinical heterogeneity, which limits...

pmc-10573502.title: Current Approach in the Management of Secondary Immunodeficiency in Patients with Hematological Malignancies: Spanish Expert Consensus Recommendations
pmc-10573502.creator: Concepción Boqué, Silvia Sánchez-Ramón, Raúl Córdoba, Carol Moreno, Elena Cabezudo, Atsushi Satake
pmc-10573502.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). A Delphi-based survey was designed to assess the opinions of clinical hematologists (n = 17) and clinical immunologists (n = 18) from across Spain on secondary immunodeficiencies (SID) in the management of oncohematological patients.

pmc-11420236.title: Acoustically semitransparent nanofibrous meshes appraised by high signal-to-noise-ratio MEMS microphones
pmc-11420236.creator: Hutomo Suryo Wasisto, Sebastian Anzinger, Giovanni Acanfora, Aloysius Farrel, Valentina Sabatini, Elisa Grimoldi, Vasco Marelli, Nikita Ovsiannikov, Konstantin Tkachuk, Giordano Tosolini, Carmine Lucignano, Marco Mietta, Guangzhao Zhang, Marc Fueldner, Erwin Peiner
pmc-11420236.description: Microelectromechanical system-based microphones demand high ingress protection levels with regard to their use in harsh environment. Here, we develop environmental protective components comprising polyimide nanofibers combined onto polyether ether ketone fabric meshes and subsequently appraise their impact on the electroacoustic properties of high signal-to-noise-ratio microelectromechanical system-based microphones via industry-standard characterizations and theoretical simulations.

pmc-12471668.title: Application of the Transition State Theory in the Study of the Osmotic Permeabilities of AQP7, AQP10 and GlpF
pmc-12471668.creator: Ruth Chan, Liao Y Chen, Mariana Ferreira
pmc-12471668.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Aquaglyceroporins, including human AQP7, AQP10, and E. coli GlpF, are known to facilitate movements of glycerol, water, and some other uncharged molecules across the cell membrane. In this study we focused on the transport of water molecules in the absence of glycerol for AQP7, AQP10 and GlpF using the Transition State Theory for the novel application of permeability and kinetics studies.

pmc-12593911.title: Treatment decision support for esophageal cancer based on PET/CT data using deep learning
pmc-12593911.creator: Qiuxiang Zheng, Fobao Lai, Zhiyong Chen
pmc-12593911.description: BackgroundMaking precise treatment decisions in esophageal cancer is essential for enhancing patient outcomes and avoiding overtreatment. Traditional approaches relying on special features or shallow learning models often fail to capture the complex, multi-scale patterns embedded in PET/CT imaging data. Recent advances in deep learning provide an opportunity to build more robust, data-driven systems for predictive modeling in oncology.

pmc-12628329.title: l‑Cysteine-Glutathione Mixed Disulfide, a Novel Bioavailable Sulfhydryl-Modified Glutathione Precursor, Protects against Early Liver Injury Induced by Short-Term Hypercholesterolemia
pmc-12628329.creator: Laura Martínez-Gili, Raquel Fucho, Francisco Caballero, Susana Núñez, Hala Saeed Jaara, Cristina Alarcón-Vila, Naira Rico, Herbert T. Nagasawa, Carmen García-Ruiz, José C. Fernández-Checa, Sandra Torres
pmc-12628329.description: Oxidative stress contributes to the damage of biological molecules and is linked to the development of multiple diseases, including liver disorders, such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). In mammals, reduced glutathione (GSH) is a pivotal antioxidant that regulates cellular responses to redox imbalances caused by reactive oxygen and nitrogen species.

pmc-12710880.title: Viral correlates of protection and the multifarious interactions of B and T cells
pmc-12710880.creator: H Cody Meissner, Peter B Gilbert, Derek Eisnor, Daniel N Wolfe
pmc-12710880.description: Validated, reproducible methods to assess immunity to a specific virus following either infection or vaccination are important for understanding susceptibility to existing and emerging infectious diseases. Correlates of protection for a specific viral illness involve humoral and cellular responses that differ by pathogen and by the portal of entry into the host.

pmc-13009037.title: Review no. 2: a beginner’s guide for calculating eGFR slope using linear mixed-effects model in R—step-by-step methods and code examples
pmc-13009037.creator: Megumi Oshima, Masahiko Gosho, Masao Iwagami, Yuka Sugawara, Hajime Nagasu, Takashige Kuwabara, Tadashi Sofue, Naoki Nakagawa, Yoshihisa Miyamoto
pmc-13009037.description: Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope, which quantifies the annual change in kidney function using longitudinal measurements of eGFR, has emerged as a critical surrogate endpoint for chronic kidney disease progression in clinical trials. Accordingly, there is an increasing number of observational studies calculating the eGFR slope as an outcome or exposure of interest.

pmc-13093250.title: A next-generation multimetal complex induces immunogenic cell death with distinct transcriptomic signatures
pmc-13093250.creator: Tomer Babu, Matthew S. Levine, Bingsong Zeng, Jonathan L. Sessler
pmc-13093250.description: In this study, a Pt(iv)–Au(i)-gemcitabine prodrug that co-releases oxaliplatin, a redox active gold N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) and gemcitabine upon intracellular reduction is reported. Relative to its constituents, this prodrug displays improved cytotoxicity, metal uptake and an in vitro immunogenic cell death response.

pmc-13155682.title: Real-world patient characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients with myelofibrosis in Japan
pmc-13155682.creator: Yusuke Yasutomi, Masashi Takano, Yi-Chen Chen, Chi-Chang Chen, Seok-Won Kim, Catherine McGuiness, Alex Slowley, Keita Kirito
pmc-13155682.description: Anemia is associated with increased morbidity, mortality, healthcare resource utilization, and costs in myelofibrosis. This longitudinal, retrospective, and descriptive cohort study used a Japanese health administrative database (Medical Data Vision) to examine treatment patterns, transfusion burden, healthcare resource utilization, and costs in patients with myelofibrosis and a subset treated with a Janus kinase inhibitor.

pmc-13186945.title: Identification of small molecule inhibitors for the Brachyspira pilosicoli glutamate racemase (Bp-MurI) enzyme using a computational and experimental approach
pmc-13186945.creator: Ravi Kant, Roberto La Ragione, Myron Christodoulides
pmc-13186945.description: Brachyspira pilosicoli (Bp) causes intestinal spirochaetosis in poultry and pigs and more rarely in humans. In this pilot study, we used a computational approach to identify potential small molecule inhibitors for the Bp glutamate racemase (Bp-MurI), an essential enzyme for cell wall biosynthesis, and then tested the Hit compounds against B. pilosicoli in a broth microdilution assay.

pmc-13354126.title: Evaluation of the effect of platelet-rich plasma on the rate of orthodontic tooth movement : A split-mouth controlled study
pmc-13354126.creator: Megha R. Revaneti, Riannee C Johnson, Azhar Mohammed, Numa Dhamnekar, M. S. Ravi
pmc-13354126.description: AIM:To evaluate the effect of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) on the rate of orthodontic tooth movement during maxillary canine retraction.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This split-mouth controlled clinical study included 15 patients aged between 18 and 30 years requiring bilateral maxillary first premolar extractions.

pmc-13394100.title: Elimination of Fusobacterium nucleatum With Biomimetic Nanoparticles to Reverse Tumor Immunosuppression and Enhance Colorectal Cancer Therapy
pmc-13394100.creator: Mengting Zhou, Jiahao Du, Cheng Li, Yefei Zhu, Kairuo Wang, Keyi Wen, Yuanyuan Zhang, Sy‐Tsong Dean Chueng, Qian Chen, Yang Zhang, Huanlong Qin

pmc-13506884.title: Artificial intelligence research in school leadership and management: a text mining-based computational literature review and future directions
pmc-13506884.creator: Turgut Karaköse, Orhun Kaptan, Gülenay Nagihan Kılıç, İbrahim Kocabaş, Ramazan Yirci
pmc-13506884.description: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in school leadership and management literature, it is important to understand not only which themes are emerging, but also how coherent, mature, and distinct these themes have become. To address this need, this study conducted a text-mining-based computational literature review of 112 articles published between 2021 and 2026.

pmc-13586831.title: Pathogen surveillance in cave-dwelling phlebotomine sand flies from Chiang Rai, northern Thailand, with the first detection of Hepatocystis
pmc-13586831.creator: Sakone Sunantaraporn, Pathamet Khositharattanakool, Kanyarat Kraivichian, Pranyu Leemingsawat, Rungfar Boonserm, Puckavadee Somwang, Padet Siriyasatien
pmc-13586831.description: Sand flies are important vectors of several pathogens of medical and veterinary significance, including Leishmania spp., Trypanosoma spp., Bartonella spp., and various arboviruses. Cave ecosystems provide suitable habitats for sand flies and often harbor large bat populations that serve as reservoirs for diverse microorganisms, potentially facilitating pathogen circulation within cave environments.
